language.script_notes: Cyrillic, Russian only on official signage (no Latin transliteration alongside). Distinguishing Russian Cyrillic from Belarusian, Ukrainian, Kazakh or Bulgarian by the alphabet alone is hard — lean on plates, road furniture and context. .ru domain, currency the ruble (₽).

road_furniture.bollard_color: Concrete or metal posts, often painted in regional colour schemes — red-and-white in some oblasts, black-and-white in others.
road_furniture.bollard_shape: Plain rounded or squared concrete post.
road_furniture.guardrail_type: Steel W-beam; long unprotected stretches on rural highways.
road_furniture.line_paint: White centre and edge lines where roads are marked; many rural roads are unmarked or unpaved.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Sign support poles are painted white with a small black band right at the base — a scheme that is essentially unique to Russia. Concrete utility poles, frequently the ex-Soviet 'holey' pole. Big blue direction signs.

architecture.roof_style: Flat roofs on Soviet apartment blocks; pitched roofs on houses; onion domes on Orthodox churches.
architecture.roof_material: Sheet metal, slate, and profiled steel; painted metal on village houses.
architecture.wall_construction: Prefabricated concrete-panel apartment blocks (panelka / khrushchyovka) in every town; log and timber village houses (izba), often with carved and painted window frames (nalichniki).
architecture.wall_color_palette: Bare grey concrete, pale yellows and greens on older blocks; blue, green and white paint on wooden houses.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Soviet panel blocks; wooden izby with carved nalichniki; onion-domed churches; dachas on city outskirts; Lenin statues and Soviet mosaics.

nature.vegetation: Vast birch, pine and spruce forest (taiga) across the centre and north, larch further east; tundra in the Arctic; wheat-and-sunflower steppe in the south.
nature.terrain: Mostly flat plains — the East European Plain and the West Siberian Plain — with the low Ural Mountains between them and higher ranges only in the south (Caucasus, Altai) and the far east.
nature.climate_signature: A great deal of the coverage is snowy, muddy or bleak, with bare birches, grey skies and low sun. Winter and shoulder-season imagery dominates.

vehicles.plate_color: Full-width white with black text, a small Russian flag and 'RUS', plus a region number in the right-hand box.
vehicles.plate_format: L NNN LL RR — one letter, three digits, two letters, then a region code (77/97/99/177/197/199/777/797/799 = Moscow; 78/98/178/198 = Saint Petersburg).
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Old boxy Ladas (VAZ) are the iconic Russia tell, alongside GAZ and UAZ. Marshrutka minibuses. In the Far East, imported right-hand-drive Japanese cars.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mostly Gen 3, with some Gen 2 and Gen 4; several distinctive camera cars, including a black car with a tall antenna.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Extensive but uneven — dense in the west, thin across Siberia and the north, with long gaps between towns. Frequently snowy or muddy.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Cyrillic, Soviet panel blocks, wooden houses, birch forest, similar road furniture
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Belarus looks tidier and better-maintained — smoother roads, mown verges, fewer potholes — uses its own plates without a region number box, and Belarusian wording sometimes appears alongside Russian.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Cyrillic, Soviet architecture, black-earth farmland and steppe in the south
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Ukrainian plates use a blue EU-style strip; Ukrainian spelling differs (і, ї, є); and Ukraine has been re-covered more recently in places.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Cyrillic, Soviet blocks, endless steppe and forest-steppe in the north
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Kazakh plates and signage (often Kazakh alongside Russian, increasingly Latin), more open and treeless steppe, and Central Asian architectural touches further south.
